answer: Persistent-label ledger. Each agent must attach a unique, sequential work label to every action; the ledger only accepts a label once, so a clone reusing its parent's history collides and is flagged. A fresh identity must start from a spent vertex (an unclaimed prior label), and labels only ripen after a full dawn-to-dawn cycle, so mass registration yields non-transferable nectar that cannot be spent until aged. Attackers pay one full cycle of idle capacity per identity plus orphaned work.
